title: DRI uncovers large-scale illegal use of SAFTA agreement in areca imports
subtitle:
Months long investigation reveals defrauding exchequer of over Rs. 2,500 crore (approx.); Rs. 75 lakh cash, 160 MT areca nuts seized (approx.); Nine arrested
Syndicates imported areca nuts into India from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and other South-East Asian countries by mis-declaring country of origin as Bangladesh
Licence of Customs Broker firm responsible for clearance of most of the fraudulent imports of areca nuts suspended
body_text:
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), in a month-long intelligence-led operation, has dismantled a major network involved in importing South-East Asian areca nuts into India by falsely declaring them as Bangladeshi origin and fraudulently availing concessional duty benefits under the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA). The investigation has so far revealed a potential revenue loss of more than Rs. 2,500 crore. Nine persons have been arrested in connection with the case.
The import of areca nuts into India attracts a Basic Customs Duty (BCD) of 100%. However, eligible imports of areca nuts made under SAFTA agreement are fully exempt from customs duty.  The areca nuts originating from Bangladesh are entitled to exemption under SAFTA if imports meet the prescribed Rules of Origin criterion.
Intelligence gathered and developed by DRI indicated that certain syndicates were fraudulently claiming the SAFTA benefits on a very large scale on imports of areca nuts.  While they were importing areca nuts originating and sourced from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and other South-East Asian countries, they were mis-declaring the country of origin of areca nuts imported into India as Bangladesh.
Thereafter, simultaneous searches were conducted at multiple premises linked to importers, Customs Brokers and IEC holders in Kolkata and Visakhapatnam. Several incriminating documents and substantial evidences establishing the South-East Asian origin of Areca nuts were recovered. DRI officers also recovered and seized around Rs. 75 lakh in cash, believed to be sale proceeds of the illegally imported goods.  A live consignment of around 160 MT of areca nuts.
The investigations so far have revealed huge scale of fraudulent imports of areca nuts in which exchequer has been duped of customs duty in excess of Rs 2,500 crore in recent years. The masterminds were facilitating the import of areca nuts from South-East Asian countries into one of the EPZ in Bangladesh and thereafter routing the goods to India merely changing containers and bags and passing them off as Bangladeshi-origin areca nuts. They had fraudulently obtained SAFTA Certificates of Origin from Bangladeshi authorities. The masterminds were charging substantial commissions from Indian importers for arranging the routing, documentation, clearance and transportation of the consignments and massive collection of payments in cash... The investigation has also brought to light the use of hawala channels and dummy entities for movement and layering of the financial proceeds.
Investigation has further revealed that one Customs Broker firm was particularly responsible for clearance of most of the fraudulent imports of areca nuts identified in the case. Consequent to the ongoing investigation by DRI, the Customs Broker's licence has been suspended by the competent authority. Nine persons have been arrested so far in connection with the case.
Such illegal imports adversely impact domestic areca nut growers and legitimate trade by creating unfair price distortion, and disrupting the level playing field for legitimate businesses. Besides causing huge loss to the Government revenue, these illegal activities also undermine regulated trade practices and economic security in the border regions.
With this operation, DRI has effectively disrupted a well-organised network involved in systematic mis-declaration of country of origin, fraudulent availment of SAFTA benefits and large-scale evasion of customs revenue.
****

enrichment.summary: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has dismantled a syndicate that fraudulently imported areca nuts from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and other South-East Asian countries into India by falsely declaring them as Bangladeshi-origin to claim duty-free benefits under the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement. The month-long operation revealed a potential revenue loss exceeding Rs. 2,500 crore, led to nine arrests, and resulted in seizure of Rs. 75 lakh cash and 160 MT of areca nuts. The syndicate routed goods through an Export Processing Zone in Bangladesh, obtained fraudulent SAFTA Certificates of Origin, and used hawala channels and dummy entities to launder proceeds; a Customs Broker firm's licence has been suspended.
enrichment.context:
Areca nuts attract a steep 100% Basic Customs Duty in India, largely to protect domestic growers, making the SAFTA exemption for genuine Bangladeshi-origin imports (which must meet Rules of Origin criteria) a significant loophole vulnerable to misuse. SAFTA, signed in 2004 among SAARC nations, aims to promote intra-regional trade through tariff concessions, but its Rules of Origin provisions—meant to ensure preferential treatment only for genuinely originating goods—are frequently exploited via transshipment fraud, where third-country goods are merely repackaged and passed off as originating from a preferential-trade partner. This case illustrates a recurring vulnerability in India's free trade agreement architecture, echoing past concerns raised by domestic industry (such as tyre, refined edible oil, and copper industries) about FTA/PTA misuse and 'origin-washing.'

The episode is also significant for India's customs enforcement and trade-remedy discourse, feeding into ongoing government efforts (e.g., CAROTAR 2020 - Rules of Origin verification rules) to tighten origin certification checks under trade agreements. It highlights the tension between trade liberalization commitments and revenue/protectionist concerns for sensitive agricultural commodities like areca nut, which is economically important for growers in Karnataka, Kerala, Assam and the Northeast.

prelims_questions.question: The South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement, referred to in the context of a recent customs fraud case, was signed under the aegis of which organization?
prelims_questions.explanation: SAFTA was signed in 2004 by member states of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) to promote intra-regional trade through tariff concessions.

prelims_questions.question: With reference to preferential trade agreements, 'Rules of Origin' primarily serve to:
options: Fix the exchange rate for imported goods
Determine the national source of a product to decide eligibility for preferential tariff treatment
Regulate the quality standards of imported goods
Set the minimum import price for anti-dumping purposes
prelims_questions.explanation: Rules of Origin criteria determine whether a good genuinely originates from a partner country under a trade agreement, preventing transshipment fraud like the one described in the DRI case.

mains_questions.question: Misuse of Rules of Origin provisions under Free Trade Agreements has become a recurring challenge for India's customs revenue and domestic industry. Discuss the issue with reference to a recent case, and suggest measures to strengthen origin verification mechanisms.

Examine how preferential trade agreements like SAFTA aim to balance regional trade promotion with the protection of domestic revenue and sensitive sectors. Illustrate with a recent example of agreement misuse.

prelims.point: Areca nut imports attract 100% Basic Customs Duty (BCD) in India, but genuine Bangladeshi-origin imports are exempt under SAFTA if Rules of Origin criteria are met.

prelims.point: Rules of Origin (RoO) are criteria used to determine the economic nationality of a product for claiming preferential tariff treatment under trade agreements.
prelims.why_important: RoO is central to CAROTAR 2020 and frequently tested as a mechanism to prevent trade agreement misuse.

prelims.point: CAROTAR 2020 (Customs Administration of Rules of Origin under Trade Agreements) rules were introduced to verify origin claims under FTAs/PTAs.
prelims.why_important: A specific enforcement mechanism aspirants should associate with FTA misuse prevention.
